# Sirach Chapter 45 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalent)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 45 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

**45:1** From Jacob came a man who found favor with everyone — beloved by God and people alike. His name was Moses, and blessed be his memory.

**45:2** God made him equal in glory to the holy ones and made him great; his enemies trembled before him.

**45:3** By his word Moses stopped the plagues; he was honored before kings; God gave him commandments for his people and showed him a portion of his glory.

**45:4** God set him apart through his faithfulness and gentleness; he chose him from among all humanity.

**45:5** He let him hear his voice, led him into the dark cloud, and gave him the commandments face to face — the law of life and knowledge — so that he could teach Jacob the covenant and enlighten Israel with God's decrees.

**45:6** He also exalted Aaron — a holy man like Moses, Moses' own brother, from the tribe of Levi.

**45:7** He made an everlasting covenant with him and gave him the priesthood over the people; he adorned him with splendor and dressed him in a glorious robe.

**45:8** He clothed him in the fullness of splendor and strengthened him with the insignia of power: the linen breeches, the long robe, and the ephod.

**45:9** He encircled him with pomegranates and many golden bells all around, to ring with every step, to fill the temple with their sound as a reminder to the Lord's people.

**45:10** He wore the sacred vestment of gold, blue, and purple — embroidered by a master's hand; the oracle of judgment, the Urim and Thummim;

**45:11** twisted scarlet — a craftsman's work; precious stones cut like seals and set in gold by a jeweler — one stone for each of the twelve tribes of Israel;

**45:12** and on his turban a gold crown engraved with the sacred inscription — glorious and distinguished, a joy to behold, beautiful beyond words.

**45:13** Nothing like this had ever existed before. No outsider ever wore it; only Aaron's sons and their descendants, forever.

**45:14** The sacrifices he offered were wholly consumed — twice every day, without interruption.

**45:15** Moses ordained him and anointed him with holy oil — an everlasting covenant for him and his descendants as long as the heavens last — to serve as priest, to praise God, and to bless his name.

**45:16** He chose him from all living people to bring offerings to the Lord: incense, pleasing aroma, a memorial offering — to make atonement for the people.

**45:17** Through the commandments he gave him authority in statutes and judgments, to teach Jacob God's testimonies and to enlighten Israel in his law.

**45:18** But outsiders ganged up on him, jealous of him in the wilderness — the followers of Dathan and Abiram, the company of Korah, in their rage and fury.

**45:19** The Lord saw it and was not pleased; they were destroyed in the heat of his anger. He worked wonders against them and consumed them in blazing fire.

**45:20** He increased Aaron's glory and gave him his inheritance; he allotted him the firstfruits of the harvest.

**45:21** He prepared food for them in plenty; they eat the offerings of the Lord — the sacrifices God gave to Aaron and his descendants.

**45:22** But in the land of the people he has no inheritance; he has no portion among them; for the Lord himself is his portion and inheritance.

**45:23** Phinehas son of Eleazar is third in glory — ablaze with zeal for the Lord. He stood his ground when the people turned away, driven by the nobility of his soul, and made atonement for Israel.

**45:24** So a covenant of peace was made with him — to lead the sanctuary and his people — so that he and his descendants would hold the dignity of the priesthood forever.

**45:25** A covenant was also made with David son of Jesse, of the tribe of Judah: the royal inheritance passes from father to son alone; and so it is with Aaron's heritage — it belongs to his descendants alone.

**45:26** May God now grant you wisdom in your heart to judge his people in righteousness — so that their prosperity never fades and their glory endures for all generations.
